question_text:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to onboard a new user. After creating the new user profile, I navigate to order an Apple Mac Book Pro for this user and complete the order. What step remains? (Select ONE.)

A. Return to the onboarding task -> add the MacBook Request (REQ) / Request Item (RITM) number in Work notes for traceability -> change the task state from Open to Closed - Complete.
B. Navigate back to the onboarding task -> write a brief summary in Additional comments for the hiring manager/requester -> click Close Task (or set state to Closed - Complete).
C. Verify the Request Item (RITM) was successfully created -> link it to the parent onboarding ticket -> then mark the onboarding task as Complete/Closed - Complete to trigger the next workflow phase.
D. Create a new hardware record -> then return to the onboarding task page and change the status/state from Open to Closed - Complete.
E. Return to the new user profile (sys_user) -> confirm the MacBook request is associated with the user/asset context -> validate provisioning details (delivery location/approvals) -> then close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.
F. Open the created MacBook request -> verify it is submitted and assigned to the correct fulfillment group -> notify the requester/manager with the tracking details -> then close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.
G. Return to the onboarding task -> reassign/hand off the task to the next fulfillment team -> set the task state to In Progress (so they can continue fulfillment).
H. Create a new hardware record -> open the MacBook request and attach the hardware record -> then send the new user a completion message and close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

### Question to answer:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to onboard a new user. After creating the new user profile, I navigate to order an Apple Mac Book Pro for this user and complete the order. What step remains? (Select ONE.)

A. Return to the onboarding task -> add the MacBook Request (REQ) / Request Item (RITM) number in Work notes for traceability -> change the task state from Open to Closed - Complete.
B. Navigate back to the onboarding task -> write a brief summary in Additional comments for the hiring manager/requester -> click Close Task (or set state to Closed - Complete).
C. Verify the Request Item (RITM) was successfully created -> link it to the parent onboarding ticket -> then mark the onboarding task as Complete/Closed - Complete to trigger the next workflow phase.
D. Create a new hardware record -> then return to the onboarding task page and change the status/state from Open to Closed - Complete.
E. Return to the new user profile (sys_user) -> confirm the MacBook request is associated with the user/asset context -> validate provisioning details (delivery location/approvals) -> then close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.
F. Open the created MacBook request -> verify it is submitted and assigned to the correct fulfillment group -> notify the requester/manager with the tracking details -> then close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.
G. Return to the onboarding task -> reassign/hand off the task to the next fulfillment team -> set the task state to In Progress (so they can continue fulfillment).
H. Create a new hardware record -> open the MacBook request and attach the hardware record -> then send the new user a completion message and close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

### Question to answer:
I am working in our ServiceNow portal. I need to assign incidents to agents with different capabilities, but when I open an incident from the Self Service incident list I do not see the "Assigned to" field. The screenshot shows the page I opened. What is the one page or view change I should use instead? Please give me only the most likely explanation or if action is needed only that one action. Do not list alternatives.

answer_gold: you should change the view to a view that exposes the Assigned to field, such as Default. you can change the view either in the list page or inside the record.
response_raw: To assign incidents to agents with different capabilities in ServiceNow, you need to navigate to the Incident Management > Incident List (Classic) view instead of the Self Service incident list. This view provides the "Assigned to" field for agent assignment.

I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My manager asks me to offboard a user named Gail-David Walker-Saunders. According to our typical workflow, what are the necessary steps?

A. Navigate to the user profile -> Unassign all hardware assets from the user -> Delete the user profile -> Mark the task as Closed - Complete.
B. Navigate to the user profile -> Delete the user profile -> Manually clear the Assigned To field on all related hardware assets -> Mark the task as Closed - Complete.
C. Navigate to Hardware Assets -> Transfer all assigned assets to Available status -> Delete the user profile -> Mark the task as Closed - Complete.
D. Delete the user profile -> Verify related incidents and tasks are reassigned -> Mark the task as Closed - Complete.
E. Navigate to the user profile -> Lock the account -> Delete the user profile -> Mark the task as Closed - Complete.
F. Navigate to the user profile -> Unassign hardware assets -> Update related records (incidents, approvals, requests) -> Delete the user profile -> Mark the task as Closed - Complete.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

question_text:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. In our company's `Managing Your Existing Expenses` workflow, after filtering Expense Lines by the target hashtag and determining which duplicate rows should be removed while keeping the most expensive duplicate, what should I do next?

A. Use a list-level bulk delete on all filtered rows.
B. Use a list-level bulk delete only on the rows chosen for removal.
C. Open each expense line chosen for removal and delete it from its record page.
D. Export the filtered rows, remove duplicates offline, and re-import them.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

I am working with our ServiceNow portal. In our company's `Managing Your Existing Expenses` workflow, after filtering Expense Lines by the target hashtag and determining which duplicate rows should be removed while keeping the most expensive duplicate, what should I do next?

A. Use a list-level bulk delete on all filtered rows.
B. Use a list-level bulk delete only on the rows chosen for removal.
C. Open each expense line chosen for removal and delete it from its record page.
D. Export the filtered rows, remove duplicates offline, and re-import them.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

response_raw: \boxed{B. Use a list-level bulk delete only on the rows chosen for removal.}
response_parsed_boxed: B. Use a list-level bulk delete only on the rows chosen for removal.

I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to allocate investments to expense lines that meet specific criteria so we can maximize returns within a given budget. Before the final action that completes the task (clicking the Update button), which meaningful action is most likely required?

A. Set the State of expense line item(s) to Closed - Complete.
B. Fill the Additional comments field and mark it as customer-visible.
C. Explain the investment methodology in the Description field.
D. Fill the Work notes field to document internal progress.
E. Set the State field expense line item(s) from Pending to Processed.
F. Set the Investment field on every expense line item.
G. Export the filtered expense lines to CSV and attach the file to the record.
H. Reassign each selected expense line to the Finance approvals queue before saving.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

question_text:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to find a report with a specific title that shows agents' performance and then create and assign problems based on it. Before assigning new problems, which single procedure is the most appropriate for locating the relevant incident report?

A. Navigate to Performance Analytics > Dashboards -> open the Incident Management dashboard -> review MTTR, SLA breaches, and workload distribution -> use the dashboard insights to decide who gets new problems.
B. Navigate to Reports > Create New -> choose table = Incident -> group by Assigned to -> add metrics (resolution time, open count, reassignment count) -> Run -> analyze results to identify underperforming agents.
C. Navigate to Reports > View/Run -> click the All (or Global) tab -> search Open Incidents by Assigned to -> open the closest match -> review current workload levels per agent.
D. Use the All filter in the left navigator -> type reports -> click View/Run -> locate and open the incident-related performance report.
E. Navigate to Reports > View/Run -> filter the report list to the Incident table -> use a contains search for #INC -> open the first result -> apply date range + Assignment group/Assigned to filters -> review the report data.
F. Navigate to Analytics Hub (or Performance Analytics) -> Dashboards -> open a Service Desk/Incident dashboard -> add a breakdown by Assigned to and a time period -> drill down into specific incidents to find bottlenecks.
G. Navigate to Reports > View/Run -> search Incident + Performance/Assignment/Resolved -> open the closest match -> then pivot/group by Assigned to and filter to Resolved/Closed in the last X days.
H. Navigate to Reports > Create New -> table = Incident -> choose Bar or Pivot -> group by Assigned to (optionally add State/Resolution time) -> set filters (Resolved/Closed + last X days + assignment group) -> Save and Run.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

### Question to answer:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to find a report with a specific title that shows agents' performance and then create and assign problems based on it. Before assigning new problems, which single procedure is the most appropriate for locating the relevant incident report?

A. Navigate to Performance Analytics > Dashboards -> open the Incident Management dashboard -> review MTTR, SLA breaches, and workload distribution -> use the dashboard insights to decide who gets new problems.
B. Navigate to Reports > Create New -> choose table = Incident -> group by Assigned to -> add metrics (resolution time, open count, reassignment count) -> Run -> analyze results to identify underperforming agents.
C. Navigate to Reports > View/Run -> click the All (or Global) tab -> search Open Incidents by Assigned to -> open the closest match -> review current workload levels per agent.
D. Use the All filter in the left navigator -> type reports -> click View/Run -> locate and open the incident-related performance report.
E. Navigate to Reports > View/Run -> filter the report list to the Incident table -> use a contains search for #INC -> open the first result -> apply date range + Assignment group/Assigned to filters -> review the report data.
F. Navigate to Analytics Hub (or Performance Analytics) -> Dashboards -> open a Service Desk/Incident dashboard -> add a breakdown by Assigned to and a time period -> drill down into specific incidents to find bottlenecks.
G. Navigate to Reports > View/Run -> search Incident + Performance/Assignment/Resolved -> open the closest match -> then pivot/group by Assigned to and filter to Resolved/Closed in the last X days.
H. Navigate to Reports > Create New -> table = Incident -> choose Bar or Pivot -> group by Assigned to (optionally add State/Resolution time) -> set filters (Resolved/Closed + last X days + assignment group) -> Save and Run.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

response_raw: \boxed{E} Navigate to Reports > View/Run -> filter the report list to the Incident table -> use a contains search for #INC -> open the first result -> apply date range + Assignment group/Assigned to filters -> review the report data.

question_text:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My manager asks me to assign N incidents to agents using predefined matching rules to ensure each incident is handled by the most suitable agent.

Which of the following shows the correct steps in order?

A. Open the Incident list -> Apply matching filters -> Assign randomly -> Close records
B. Open the correct Incident list -> Clear existing filters -> Apply matching rules -> Enable Show Related Fields -> Verify results -> Bulk edit assignments -> Validate
C. Export incidents -> Edit in Excel -> Re-import -> Notify agents
D. Find and open one incident that needs edits -> Apply matching rules -> Edit assignments -> Repeat for all N incidents
E. Ask another agent to assign incidents -> Review later -> Update if needed

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My manager asks me to assign N incidents to agents using predefined matching rules to ensure each incident is handled by the most suitable agent.

Which of the following shows the correct steps in order?

A. Open the Incident list -> Apply matching filters -> Assign randomly -> Close records
B. Open the correct Incident list -> Clear existing filters -> Apply matching rules -> Enable Show Related Fields -> Verify results -> Bulk edit assignments -> Validate
C. Export incidents -> Edit in Excel -> Re-import -> Notify agents
D. Find and open one incident that needs edits -> Apply matching rules -> Edit assignments -> Repeat for all N incidents
E. Ask another agent to assign incidents -> Review later -> Update if needed

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

response_raw: \boxed{B} Open the correct Incident list > Clear existing filters > Apply matching rules > Enable Show Related Fields > Verify results > Bulk edit assignments > Validate

\boxed{2}

### Question to answer:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to manage expenses whose short descriptions contain a hashtag tag. What is the correct step to find the matching expenses on the Expense Line page by opening the saved smart filter for that hashtag?

Mark your final answer in \boxed{}.

answer_gold: There is no saved smart filter for that hashtag in the traced workflow.
response_raw:
\boxed{To find the matching expenses on the Expense Line page by opening the saved smart filter for a specific hashtag, follow these steps:

1. Navigate to the Expense Lines page using the "Expenses" or "Finance" menu in your ServiceNow portal.
2. Click on the "More menus" button (usually located at the top left corner of the screen).
3. In the dropdown menu, click on "Scope selectors".
4. In the "Choose search context" dropdown, select "Expense Lines".
5. In the "Search" field, enter your specific hashtag (e.g., #SERIES-df9c3c1e-3).
6. Press Enter or click on the magnifying glass icon to perform the search.
7. The system will display a list of Expense Lines whose short descriptions contain the specified hashtag. You can then open each record by clicking on them.}
response_parsed_boxed:
To find the matching expenses on the Expense Line page by opening the saved smart filter for a specific hashtag, follow these steps:

1. Navigate to the Expense Lines page using the "Expenses" or "Finance" menu in your ServiceNow portal.
2. Click on the "More menus" button (usually located at the top left corner of the screen).
3. In the dropdown menu, click on "Scope selectors".
4. In the "Choose search context" dropdown, select "Expense Lines".
5. In the "Search" field, enter your specific hashtag (e.g., #SERIES-df9c3c1e-3).
6. Press Enter or click on the magnifying glass icon to perform the search.
7. The system will display a list of Expense Lines whose short descriptions contain the specified hashtag. You can then open each record by clicking on them.

F. Set the description field to `duplicate`
G. Set it to `resolved as duplicate` and include timestamp + assignee initials

### Question to answer:
I am working in our ServiceNow portal. I am off-boarding a user and trying to de-assign the user from their hardware, but after I click in the field as shown in the screenshot, click "Update", and reopen the record, the same user is still assigned. What is the most likely issue or one action I should take? Please give me only the most likely explanation or if action is needed only that one action. Do not list alternatives.

answer_gold: the field was not actually cleared; manually remove the assigned user value (for example by pressing Backspace) and then click Update.
response_raw: The most likely issue is that the offboarding process might not have been properly completed, or there could be a delay in the system for the changes to take effect. To resolve this issue, you should ensure that the user's offboarding process has been finalized and all related tasks (such as de-provisioning access) have been completed. After completing the offboarding process, try reassigning the hardware again. If the problem persists, consider reaching out to your ServiceNow administrator for assistance.

I am working in our ServiceNow portal. I need to order the same item as someone else did, but after finding the item from Requested Items I do not see an entry point to place the new order. The screenshot shows the page I am on. What is the one thing I should do next? Please give me only the most likely explanation or if action is needed only that one action. Do not list alternatives.

answer_gold: should use the filter inside the "All" tab on the top left corner to find the service catalog module.
response_raw: To place a new order for an item from Requested Items, you need to submit a request for the same item. Since there's no direct entry point to place a new order on this page, you should click on the item's name (for example, 'Dell Latitude E6420') and then navigate to the 'Request' tab or create a new request from the ServiceNow homepage.

### Question to answer:
I am working in our ServiceNow portal to offboard a user. I opened this page, cleared the "Assigned to" field, updated the record, and returned to the list, but the user still appears assigned and the hardware is still assigned. The screenshot shows this state. What is the most likely explanation or one action I should take? Please give me only the most likely explanation or if action is needed only that one action. Do not list alternatives.

answer_gold: 1) the page you are looking at is not wrong; 2) inside the record, clearing the "Assigned to" field is not enough, you need to click into that field and then click elsewhere so the cleared value is actually applied before updating.
response_raw: The most likely explanation for the user and hardware asset still appearing assigned is that the reference field "Assigned to" was cleared but the underlying sys_id of the user record was not updated. To resolve this issue, you should update the "Assigned to" field again using the lookup UI (magnifying glass) to re-set/clear the reference in a way that properly updates the stored sys_id.
response_parsed_boxed: The most likely explanation for the user and hardware asset still appearing assigned is that the reference field "Assigned to" was cleared but the underlying sys_id of the user record was not updated. To resolve this issue, you should update the "Assigned to" field again using the lookup UI (magnifying glass) to re-set/clear the reference in a way that properly updates the stored sys_id.

Since no new fields related to the deleted records count appear in the observed pages, I cannot provide a definitive answer for this question.

D. Sales Laptop
E. Standard Laptop

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

response_raw:
\boxed{Six}

question_text:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. In our company's tight-window, priority-aware change-request rescheduling workflow, which combined rule is correct?

A. Schedule higher-risk changes first, and keep the gap between consecutive changes to at most 1 day while honoring risk-based durations.
B. Keep the original change order and only resize durations by risk, even if adjacent changes overlap.
C. Schedule higher-impact changes first, and keep the gap between consecutive changes to at most 1 day while honoring risk-based durations.
D. Schedule lower-impact changes first so high-impact requests can use spare time at the end of the window.
E. Schedule higher-impact changes first, keep the gap between consecutive changes to at most 1 hour, and still honor risk-based durations.
F. Ignore the gap-limit requirement and only ensure non-overlap plus risk-based durations.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

I am working with our ServiceNow portal. In our company's tight-window, priority-aware change-request rescheduling workflow, which combined rule is correct?

A. Schedule higher-risk changes first, and keep the gap between consecutive changes to at most 1 day while honoring risk-based durations.
B. Keep the original change order and only resize durations by risk, even if adjacent changes overlap.
C. Schedule higher-impact changes first, and keep the gap between consecutive changes to at most 1 day while honoring risk-based durations.
D. Schedule lower-impact changes first so high-impact requests can use spare time at the end of the window.
E. Schedule higher-impact changes first, keep the gap between consecutive changes to at most 1 hour, and still honor risk-based durations.
F. Ignore the gap-limit requirement and only ensure non-overlap plus risk-based durations.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

response_raw: \boxed{C} Schedule higher-impact changes first, and keep the gap between consecutive changes to at most 1 day while honoring risk-based durations.

answer_gold: the list header search requires a left-side wildcard; use `*#tag` so the left-side `*` is applied for contains-style matching.
response_raw: The most likely issue here is that the wildcard character (*) is not being recognized in the search box for Expense Lines. If this does not work, it may be necessary to check the system settings or consult with your ServiceNow administrator for assistance.

I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to manage expenses whose short descriptions contain the hashtag tag `#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3`. What is the correct step to find the matching expenses on the Expense Line page?

A. Click `Show Filter` on the Expense Line list, add condition `Short description` `contains` `#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3`, then click `Run`.
B. Use the list search dropdown, choose `Short description`, enter `#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3`, and press Enter.
C. Use the list search dropdown, choose `Short description`, enter `*#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3`, and press Enter.
D. Use the Short Description column search box and enter `#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3` directly.
E. Open filter builder and set `Short description` `starts with` `#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3`.
F. Open filter builder and set `Short description` `is` `#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3`.
G. Use global search for `#SERIES-df9c3c1e-3`, then filter results to Expense Lines.
H. Right-click a Short description value and choose `Filter Out` to narrow results.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.
